Japan.Marshall_air: Coherent local strike capacity is effectively gone. A handful of dispersed reconnaissance/water/local-defense aircraft remain at outer nodes; some westward evacuation/ferry attempts occur, but no new mass attack package is generated.
Japan.outer_sensor_net: Maloelap/Wotje/Mili/Jaluit and westward relay nodes remain able to observe/report at operational level, though repeated US suppression degrades sortie and transmitter availability.

submarines.decision: Close Kwajalein penetration is terminated as target density falls and ASW remains maximal.
submarines.disposition: Roughly three-to-four still-useful boats shift toward outer reporting/withdrawal and possible Eniwetok approach lanes; damaged/fatigued boats withdraw west. No automatic final compensation hit is created.
submarines.last_8_10Feb_center: No additional major US ship hit.

Japan.carrier_force: Shokaku, Zuikaku and Soryu continue westward regeneration. Hiryu remains propulsion-capable but requires deck/air-group repair and reorganization; no Marshall return is centered. The four-deck hull advantage survives, but carrier-air cadre debt sharply limits immediate renewed strike generation.

US.TF58: Cabot remains campaign-out. Other fast decks are physically available subject to aircraft replacement, maintenance, fuel and aircrew regeneration. Majuro remains the main immediate replenishment node.
US.amphibious_force: Ground victory begins releasing heavy support, CVE and DD wallets, but shipping/landing-craft turnaround and ASW prevent instantaneous follow-on assault.
US.next_operations: HAILSTONE- and CATCHPOLE-equivalent dates remain OPEN and must be recomputed from replenishment, air-group replacement, assault-shipping turnaround, Japanese warning/evacuation and Eniwetok adaptation rather than inherited historical dates.
